key_insight: The paper shows that interpretable linear meta-learning plus adaptive uncertainty calibration can improve multi-objective chemical search under tight data and compute limits.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical framework for accelerating early-stage molecular discovery with surrogate models that are both explainable and better suited to active optimization than standard deep learning approaches.
method: Modular EGO pipeline for multi-objective molecular discovery
Linear meta-learning surrogates trained across chemical objectives and cheap auxiliary properties
Adaptive-confidence uncertainty tuning to rebalance exploration vs. exploitation during search
evidence_signal: On a real large-scale search for spin-crossover metal-organic complexes, the baseline was 78% worse in Pareto sense, and dynamic confidence tuning outperformed more than 50% of the statically calibrated front.
watch_item: Performance depends on calibration quality and transferability; if the auxiliary tasks or confidence updates are poorly chosen, the search may over-explore or miss rare high-value candidates.
paper_title: Interpretable Meta-Learning for Multi-Objective Chemical Search
